_**Come Away with Me**_ is the debut album by American recording artist Norah Jones, released on February 26, 2002, by Blue Note Records. Recording sessions took place at Sorcerer Sound Studio in New York City and Allaire Studios in Shokan, New York.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4)

_Come Away with Me_ peaked at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200 chart and received Grammy Awards for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-AwardsAllmusic-10) It was later certified Diamond by the RIAA on February 15, 2005, for shipments of over ten million copies in the United States,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-RIAA-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Lipshutz-12) and has sold over 27 million copies worldwide as of 2016, making it one of the best-selling albums of all time,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-McCormick-13) the best-selling debut album by a female artist of all time, and the second best-selling album of the 21st century.
Audio 3[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Don't_Know_Why_sample.ogg "Play audio")Duration: 18 seconds.

_Come Away with Me_ is an acoustic pop and blues pop[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-z349-5) album that features Jones supported by Kevin Breit, Bill Frisell, Adam Levy, Adam Rogers, and Tony Scherr on guitar; Sam Yahel on organ; Jenny Scheinman on violin; Rob Burger on accordion; and Brian Blade, Dan Rieser, and Kenny Wollesen on drums —all jazz musicians with a leaning to Americana. The recording of _Come Away with Me_ started on September 20, 2000 and ended in December 2001. Jones wrote the title song. Guitarist Jesse Harris wrote "Don't Know Why". The album includes Jones' versions of "The Nearness of You" by Hoagy Carmichael and "Cold, Cold Heart" by Hank Williams,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4) the former deliberately chosen to be the closing track to the album by producer Arif Mardin.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-14)
_Come Away with Me_ incorporates blues, jazz,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-:0-15)folk, soul, and country.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4) Bobby Dodd of _All About Jazz_ writes that although the album features jazz standards, jazz purists and academics "may deny [Jones] jazz credibility for her folk infusion".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-16)

## Commercial performance
[edit]
_Come Away with Me_ debuted at number 139 on the US _Billboard_ 200 upon its release in February 2002 selling 10,000 copies in its first week.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-post-18) Despite being released at a time when music piracy was high and album sales were declining,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-variety9-1-2003-19) the album was certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) in August that same year.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-RIAA-11) The album eventually climbed to the top of the _Billboard_ 200 in January 2003, almost a year after it was released selling 108,000 copies that week.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Billboard_2003-20) By the time of the Grammy Awards the following month, _Come Away with Me_ had already sold 3 million copies in the country.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-bb2007-21) Jones' success at the award show resulted in the album moving another 600,000 copies the week immediately following the awards.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-bb2007-21) CDs of the album were sold at Starbucks stores and at a retail price of $9.99, lower than most albums at the time.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-22) In total,

## Commercial performance
_Come Away with Me_ received acclaim from music critics. At Metacritic, which assigns a normalized rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream critics, the album has an average score of 82 out of 100, which indicates "universal acclaim" based on 9 reviews.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-MC-28)
The album received 3.5 out of 4 stars from both the _Chicago Sun-Times_ and the _Los Angeles Times_ reviews.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-CST-30)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-LATimes-34)AllMusic's David R. Adler wrote that "while the mood of this record stagnates after a few songs, it does give a strong indication of Jones' alluring talents."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-allmusic-29)Robert Christgau of _The Village Voice_ cited it as "the most unjazz album [Blue Note] has ever released" and criticized that "Jones's voice dominates the record."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Christgau-38)
_The A.V. Club_ gave it a favorable review and called the album "A showcase for Jones' remarkable voice, the disc captures a singer whose rare instinct for interpretation always serves the song, rather than working against it."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-39)_E! Online_ gave it an A and stated: "Gorgeous and intimate, the 14 songs on her debut disc ache with romantic maturity and a smart, slow-jam sexiness that belies the fact that, at 22, Jones is hardly older than Britney Spears."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-MC-28)

## Commercial performance
_Kludge_ included it on their list of best albums of 2002.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-40)Mark Beaumont, writing for _NME_ in 2016, included it on his list of eight of the all-time best-selling albums in the UK that have no redeeming features whatsoever, dubbing it "soporific, simplistic jazz wallpaper muzak".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-41)

March 18, 2022
20 years ago in 2002, Norah Jones released her debut **_Come Away With Me_**, an unassuming album would go on to charm the world and introduce one of the greatest voices of our time. The album steadily grew into a global phenomenon, reaching #1 in 20 countries, selling nearly 30 million copies, and sweeping the 2003 GRAMMY Awards with eight wins including Album of the Year, Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best New Artist. On April 29, Blue Note will release **_Come Away With Me: 20th Anniversary Super Deluxe Edition_**, a remarkable 44-track collection that captures the emergence of a singular talent and reveals for the first time the full story of the making of this now-classic album.
In addition to a remaster of the original album, which was produced by **Arif Mardin**, the _Super Deluxe Edition_ also includes 22 previously unreleased tracks including the original demos that Norah submitted to Blue Note which featured a remarkably self-assured version of the jazz standard “**Spring Can Really Hang You Up The Most**” that Norah had recorded in her high school band room accompanying herself on piano. Also included are the complete _First Session_ demos she made after being signed and the first version of the album that Norah made at Allaire Studios with producer **Craig Street**, most of which has never been heard before and offers a fascinating look at the album that might have been.

The _20th Anniversary Super Deluxe Edition_ was produced by **Eli Wolf** and will be released digitally and physically as a 4-LP vinyl set and a 3-CD set, both of which come in premium packaging with an extensive booklet featuring new liner notes by Norah and rare session photos. _Come Away with Me_ peaked at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200 chart and received Grammy Awards for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-AwardsAllmusic-10) It was later certified Diamond by the RIAA on February 15, 2005, for shipments of over ten million copies in the United States,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-RIAA-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Lipshutz-12) and has sold over 27 million copies worldwide as of 2016, making it one of the best-selling albums of all time,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-McCormick-13) the best-selling debut album by a female artist of all time, and the second best-selling album of the 21st century.

_Come Away with Me_ is an acoustic pop and blues pop[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-z349-5) album that features Jones supported by Kevin Breit, Bill Frisell, Adam Levy, Adam Rogers, and Tony Scherr on guitar; Sam Yahel on organ; Jenny Scheinman on violin; Rob Burger on accordion; and Brian Blade, Dan Rieser, and Kenny Wollesen on drums —all jazz musicians with a leaning to Americana. The recording of _Come Away with Me_ started on September 20, 2000 and ended in December 2001. Jones wrote the title song. Guitarist Jesse Harris wrote "Don't Know Why". The album includes Jones' versions of "The Nearness of You" by Hoagy Carmichael and "Cold, Cold Heart" by Hank Williams,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4) the former deliberately chosen to be the closing track to the album by producer Arif Mardin.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-14)
_Come Away with Me_ incorporates blues, jazz,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-:0-15)folk, soul, and country.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4) Bobby Dodd of _All About Jazz_ writes that although the album features jazz standards, jazz purists and academics "may deny [Jones] jazz credibility for her folk infusion".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-16)

March 18, 2022
20 years ago in 2002, Norah Jones released her debut **_Come Away With Me_**, an unassuming album would go on to charm the world and introduce one of the greatest voices of our time. The album steadily grew into a global phenomenon, reaching #1 in 20 countries, selling nearly 30 million copies, and sweeping the 2003 GRAMMY Awards with eight wins including Album of the Year, Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best New Artist. On April 29, Blue Note will release **_Come Away With Me: 20th Anniversary Super Deluxe Edition_**, a remarkable 44-track collection that captures the emergence of a singular talent and reveals for the first time the full story of the making of this now-classic album.
In addition to a remaster of the original album, which was produced by **Arif Mardin**, the _Super Deluxe Edition_ also includes 22 previously unreleased tracks including the original demos that Norah submitted to Blue Note which featured a remarkably self-assured version of the jazz standard “**Spring Can Really Hang You Up The Most**” that Norah had recorded in her high school band room accompanying herself on piano. Also included are the complete _First Session_ demos she made after being signed and the first version of the album that Norah made at Allaire Studios with producer **Craig Street**, most of which has never been heard before and offers a fascinating look at the album that might have been.

The album includes Jones' versions of "The Nearness of You" by Hoagy Carmichael and "Cold, Cold Heart" by Hank Williams,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4) the former deliberately chosen to be the closing track to the album by producer Arif Mardin.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-14)
_Come Away with Me_ incorporates blues, jazz,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-:0-15)folk, soul, and country.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-Adler-4) Bobby Dodd of _All About Jazz_ writes that although the album features jazz standards, jazz purists and academics "may deny [Jones] jazz credibility for her folk infusion".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Away_with_Me#cite_note-16)

20 years ago in 2002, Norah Jones released her debut **_Come Away With Me_**, an unassuming album would go on to charm the world and introduce one of the greatest voices of our time. Also included are the complete _First Session_ demos she made after being signed and the first version of the album that Norah made at Allaire Studios with producer **Craig Street**, most of which has never been heard before and offers a fascinating look at the album that might have been.
